title: Who’s in, Who’s Out? Analyzing the USMNT’s Depth Chart After Perfect Fall Window
subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Sophia Vesely, Amanda LangellOct 11, 2026The U.S. has been in fine form since the World Cup. / Kohjiro Kinno/Sports IllustratedU.S. men’s national team manager Mauricio Pochettino has trialed no shortage of stars, yet only some have made their mark donning the red, white and blue.

The 2030 World Cup might still be four years away, but every international break is a chance for Pochettino to zero in on his best squad, one capable of finally making a deep run on the biggest stage in soccer. From established veterans to exciting, unproven teenagers, the Argentine boss has plenty of talent at his disposal—but where do they all stack up?

Sports Illustrated’s deep dive into the USMNT’s depth breaks down the Stars and Stripes’ best players at every position. The guide only includes players that have been rostered in the last 12 months, dating back to October 2025. Former captain Tim Ream is excluded following his retirement.

The rankings are not only based off current success, but also level of potential, especially when it comes to young players like Brooklyn Raines, Neil Pierre and Mathis Albert, all of whom have a high ceiling.

Brian Schwake is in line to be the USMNT No. 1 moving forward. / Brace Hemmelgarn/USSF/Getty ImagesBrian Schwake (Nashville SC)Diego Kochen (Lyngby)Chris Brady (Chicago Fire)Matt Freese (NYCFC)Patrick Schulte (Columbus Crew)Roman Celentano (FC Cincinnati)Jonathan Klinsmann (Cesena)Matt Turner (New England Revolution)At the 2026 World Cup, it was Matt Freese between the posts for the USMNT. But a disastrous outing against Belgium was the final straw for the inconsistent, mistake-prone goalkeeper. He might’ve still logged 45 minutes against Peru this fall, but he soon watched three other names jump above his on the depth chart.

Chris Brady and Diego Kochen both got looks this camp, but the latter made the better impression. Kochen played the full 90 minutes and kept a clean sheet in the team’s 3–0 win against Mexico. The 20-year-old also became the youngest goalkeeper to ever start a game for the USMNT.

Still, it’s Brian Schwake who emerged from the international window as the favorite to become Pochettino’s No. 1. The American shot-stopper has had a fantastic season with Supporters’ Shield favorites Nashville SC and was the only goalkeeper to make two starts for the USMNT this fall.
Schwake has a ways to go before he truly proves himself capable of locking down top attacks on the international stage, but he’s no doubt leading the race at the moment.

Alex Freeman was a breakout star at the World Cup. / Robin Alam/ISI Photos/ISI Photos/Getty ImagesAlex Freeman (Villarreal)Antonee Robinson (Fulham)Peyton Miller (New England Revolution)Joe Scally (Borussia Mönchengladbach)Francis Westfield (Philadelphia Union)John Tollkin (Holstein Kiel)Fullback is no longer a problem position for the USMNT. The ever-reliable and experienced Antonee Robinson owns the left flank while breakout star Alex Freeman commands the right.

Freeman’s impressive form for Orlando City earned him a place in Pochettino’s squad last year and he quickly became a starter. There were doubts over whether he could hang with the best at the World Cup, but the 22-year-old, who had since made the move to Villarreal, silenced all doubters this summer—and continued his strong form during the team’s fall friendlies.

Joe Scally is the man tasked with the near-impossible job of displacing Freeman, much like Peyton Miller’s uphill battle trying to take minutes from Robinson. But the latter is gaining Premier League attention after his first senior camp and at age 18, his career is just beginning.

Chris Richards is the leader of Mauricio Pochettino’s defense.  / Taylor Banner/USSF/Getty ImagesChris Richards (Crystal Palace)Auston Trusty (Celtic)Mark McKenzie (Toulouse)George Campbell (West Bromwich Albion)Neil Pierre (Philadelphia Union)Miles Robinson (FC Cincinnati)Cameron Carter-Vickers (Celtic)There’s no shortage of center backs at Pochettino’s disposal, but the long list of names are all essentially fighting for one spot. Chris Richards is irreplaceable in the USMNT’s XI; the Crystal Palace standout is the team’s defensive leader, both on and off the pitch.

There is a Ream-shaped hole alongside him in central defense. Auston Trusty’s experience with the USMNT and playing in Europe at the club level makes him the most trustworthy—no pun intended—option for Pochettino. He is also versatile enough to play at left back as well.

Keep an eye out for Pierre, though. The 18-year-old got his first call-up this fall and is billed by many to be the best long-term option to replace Ream. The towering center back is brilliant in the air and has a knack for goal, but he has plenty of growing to do before he is strong enough to beat out Trusty, Mark McKenzie or George Campbell.

Tyler Adams is the new USMNT captain. / Luke Hales/Getty ImagesTyler Adams (Bournemouth)Weston McKennie (Juventus)Sebastian Berhalter (Middlesbrough)Johnny Cardoso (Atlético Madrid)Brooklyn Raines (New England Revolution)Yunus Musah (AC Milan)Tanner Tessmann (Lyon)Aidan Morris (Middlesbrough)Timothy Tillman (LAFC)James Sands (NYCFC)Cristian Roldan (Seattle Sounders)Pochettino experimented with multiple formations during the most recent four friendlies, but there was always one constant: The Argentine boss deployed two defensive midfielders.

New captain Tyler Adams is a lock in the middle of the park, but his partner in Pochettino’s double pivot is up for grabs. Weston McKennie has the pedigree and the World Cup experience, but his absence this fall allowed other players to stand out.

Sebastian Berhalter staked the biggest claim for a starting role moving forward, continuing his impressive rise with the USMNT ever since his breakout 2025 Gold Cup campaign. There is a wealth of competition, though.

The young Brooklyn Raines started two of the USMNT’s four wins during the September-October break and played beyond his 21 years. His defensive prowess outranks what Yunus Musah has brought lately, and he has better vision with the ball at his feet than Tanner Tessmann.

Johnny Cardoso is arguably more well-rounded than all three of the aforementioned options, but he has to get himself back into Pochettino’s plans after missing the 2026 World Cup with an ankle injury.
